RSpec is part of 4 of my public repositories, from 2014 to 2015.

What it was for: [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (2), [Systems and infrastructure](@/projects/systems.md) (1) and [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (1).

Most recently: [csv2psql](@/work/csv2psql.md): Turns CSV into insert or update statements for PostgreSQL; [apollon](@/work/apollon.md): Your own personal cluster built on top of the cloud; [gooddata\_connectors\_metadata](@/work/gooddata-connectors-metadata.md): The gem for accessing metadata for gooddata connector infrastructure.

2 of these projects run as live sites.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses RSpec: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links RSpec to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
